newsitem.title: MEXICO: U.S. to revamp some affirmative action programs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to revamp some affirmative action programs.

text.p: The United States this week will publish rules changing some federal affirmative action procurement programmes, possibly hurting some minority-owned firms while helping others, a U.S. official said on Tuesday.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry, speaking during a state visit of U.S. President Bill Clinton to Mexico, told reporters the Justice Department had sent the proposed regulations to the U.S. federal register for publication this week.

"The Justice Department has forwarded to the register a proposed 'reg' that will actually implement some changes in federal affirmative action programmes that we believe will be necessary to defend those programmes in court under the constitutional criteria established by Adarand," McCurry said.

He was referring to a 1995 Supreme Court decision that found that federal affirmative action procurement programmes were constitutional but that they must be narrowly tailored and serve a compelling need.
In the case, Adarand Constructors Inc., a white-owned Colorado highway construction firm, had challenged the award of a contract to a minority-owned business.

"The president is very comfortable that mending, and not ending, is the way also to preserve and protect these programmes as they face new constitutional, and ultimately political, scrutiny," McCurry added.

Another U.S. official said that the proposed rules would require the federal government to take a new approach to the award of such contracts, undertaking an industry review to decide where minority-owned companies face discrimination.
The official said the new system might hurt such companies in industries where there did not appear to be discrimination, while helping those in which minority firms were under-represented.
